text: A bookmark saves the exact state of an entire report page — not just which page, but its filters, its slicer selections, its sort order, even which visuals are currently showing. Here's how to actually put that to work in a real report.
Turn on the Bookmarks pane from the View ribbon, get the page looking precisely the way you want it remembered — filters set, the right visuals visible — and select Add.

Power BI names the new bookmark automatically, so rename it right away to something meaningful you'll actually recognize later. And under that bookmark's More options, you control exactly what it restores: Data for filters and slicer selections, Display for visual visibility, and Current page for whether selecting it navigates somewhere specific or just applies wherever you already are. Turn Data off if you're using bookmarks to switch between different visual layouts rather than different filtered views.

The real payoff shows up once a bookmark is attached to something clickable. Insert a button, toggle its Action on, set Type to Bookmark, and pick the specific one you want — now selecting that button resets filters or switches an entire view, in exactly one click, for anyone viewing the report.

Group several bookmarks together under More options, Group, and selecting View on any one of them plays just that group as a slideshow — a fully guided walkthrough, stepping an audience through a sequence of insights with nobody touching anything themselves. Last lesson of the chapter: analytics, forecasting, and advanced visuals.
